The Good Ride review — Carving: "a lot of pop and spring out of the turn... really fun board to turn on the hill" (rated Carving: Great) [50] 106. The Good Ride review — Speed: "Good glide to the base and good dampness at speed" (rated Speed: Great) [51] 107. The Good Ride review — Powder: "No thanks... not ideal" for powder (rated Powder: Poor) [52] 108. The Good Ride review — Switch: "Very doable either way when centered up" (rated Switch: Great) [53] 109. The Good Ride review — Overall: "board that isn't for everyone but has appeal to the technical/old school rider" [58] 114. Snowboard Robot review — "very similar feel to the Burton Custom (camber version)" [60] 116. Snowboard Robot review — Turn initiation: "very smooth and easy, and the grip the whole way through the turn feels very strong" [61] 117. Snowboard Robot review — Flex feel: "Not too soft, not too stiff" at about 72kg rider weight [62] 118. Snowboard Robot review — Waist width caution: "narrow waist widths, they could be an issue if you have bigger boots" [63] 119. Snowboarding Profiles review — "Carves really well and good at speed but isn't so aggressive that you feel like you have to push it hard all the time" [64] 120. Snowboarding Profiles review — "A good do-it-all board, on the more aggressive side of the playful to aggressive scale" [65] 121. Snowboarding Profiles — categorizes it as "aggressive all-mountain snowboard" [66] 122. Whitelines review (2015/16) — "responsive and grippy with a nice playful flex that lets you pop and butter all over" [67] 123. Whitelines review — "great board for anyone brought up on rockered boards that wants to get to know what a proper twin camber snowboard can do" [68] FORUM USER OPINIONS 124. Forum: Team described as "a great midflex camber board. Fun carving and popping around the resort" [69] 125. Forum: Dual degressive sidecut gives "more forgiving turn initiation than the Custom" [70] 126. Forum: One user "found the team surprisingly soft. Couldn't push it that hard at all" — prefers Team Pro for carving [71] 127. Forum: Team was compared to Burton Custom — "on paper they seem very similar" [72] 128. Forum: User chose Team over Custom due to: wider Wide option, no channel system, lower price [73] 129. Forum: Nitro Team's dual-degressive sidecut "would be less catchy" than Burton Custom's sidecut [74] 130. Forum: "If I wanted a single all mountain board, the Custom (camber) and the Nitro Team(s) would be at the top of my list" [75] 131. Forum: One user ended up selling Team Pro in favor of Bataleon Goliath and Ride Algorythm [76] COMPETITOR COMPARISONS 132. Comparable boards: Burton Custom (camber), CAPiTA Mercury, Salomon Assassin, K2 Broadcast, Yes Standard, Jones Mountain Twin [77] 133. vs. Burton Custom: Team is slightly softer; Custom is "slightly stiffer... more reactive when you press on the sidecut" [78] 134. vs. Nitro Team Pro: Team Pro adds Carbon Tape, Sintered Speed Formula II base (faster), and 8/10 flex vs 7/10 [79] 135. Team Pro USD MSRP (2026): $629.95 at evo [80] 136. Nitro Beast is the stiffest option in the lineup (rated 8/10 but feels stiffer) [81] 137. Budget alternative within Nitro lineup: Phase at $459.95 [82] RELATED MODELS & LINE HISTORY 138. Predecessor: The Nitro Team has been continuously produced for over 20 years with incremental updates [11] 139. The Team previously offered a "Gullwing" (hybrid camber) variant; discontinued after 2023 model [83] 140. Team Pro variant: pro-level version with carbon reinforcement and faster base [42] 141. Future Team: youth version of the Team [84] 142. Team Pro x Marcus Kleveland: pro signature edition ($649.95 MSRP) [85] DESIGN DETAILS 143. Nose design: "semi-blunted tips" with slightly longer nose than tail for powder float [43] 144. Setback: -1.5cm across all sizes (consistent) [1] (merchant verified) 145. Board weight: Feels normal/average according to The Good Ride [86] 146. Board profile description: Directional Twin Shape "combines the look and feel of a true twin with the versatility of a directional board" [87] PRODUCT LIFECYCLE 147. Model first sold: The Team model has been in the Nitro lineup since at least the early 2000s (over two decades) [11] 148. Current model release date: 2027 model on preorder for May 2026 delivery [1] 149. Nitro typically releases new model years in spring/summer for the following winter season [unverified — industry standard] KEY PURCHASE CONSIDERATIONS 150. One-board quiver potential: Strong — frequently recommended as a "do-it-all" board [59][64] 151. Weakness in powder: Consistent across all reviewers — full camber and minimal setback limits float [52][88] 152. Narrow waist width on standard sizes: Potential issue for boot sizes US 10+ [63] 153. Value proposition: Generally priced $50-100 lower than comparable Burton Custom [27][73] 154. Resale value: Lower than Burton; "Burton is the one brand that holds resale" per forum discussion [89] 155. No carbon reinforcement (unlike Team Pro) — keeps price lower but less pop/response [42]
